headline: Iran to declare new 'controlled zone' outside Strait of Hormuz, warns of sanctions for entry
summary: Iran's top security official announced a new controlled zone outside the Strait of Hormuz, warning that any vessel entering it will face sanctions. This move follows the closure of the Strait after a US-Israel attack.
details: Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, has announced that Iran will declare a new 'controlled zone' outside the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that the official declaration would be made within a few days.

Rezaei, who serves as a military advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Ali Khamenei, explained that the new zone would commence from where the US naval blockade began. It is expected to span various areas of the Gulf.

He issued a stern warning that any vessel attempting to enter this newly designated controlled zone would be added to a sanctions list. This declaration signals a significant escalation in regional maritime control.
Rezaei also revealed that a new international corridor for ship movement through the Strait of Hormuz has been established. This arrangement was finalized in consultation with Oman.

He confirmed that Iran would be responsible for operating this new corridor, with an official announcement anticipated in the coming days. The Strait of Hormuz is critically important, typically facilitating the transport of approximately one-fifth of the world's total oil and gas supply.

Tehran had previously closed the Strait of Hormuz on February 28, following an attack on Iran by the US and Israel. This closure has already had a noticeable impact on the global energy market, contributing to increased prices.
Separately, US President Donald Trump is reportedly considering renaming the Strait of Hormuz. International media outlets suggest he intends to rename the strategic waterway 'Trump Strait'.

headline_marked: [[Ukraine war could last until winter]], Zelenskyy tells Trump's envoys in Kyiv
headline: Ukraine war could last until winter, Zelenskyy tells Trump's envoys in Kyiv
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with Donald Trump's top envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, in Kyiv, discussing peace efforts and the conflict's potential duration.
details: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that the ongoing war with Russia could extend until winter. He made this statement after a meeting in Kyiv with two top envoys of former US President Donald Trump.

The envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, visited Ukraine for the first time since Russia's full-scale invasion began. Prior to their Kyiv discussions, they held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday.

Witkoff described the Sunday discussions in Kyiv, aimed at ending the war, as "important" and "fruitful," expressing optimism for a resolution. He stated confidence in a good outcome and noted "much progress" in the Moscow talks with Russian representatives.

Zelenskyy emphasized that if the war continues into winter, Ukraine would require significant assistance for its air defense system and energy sector. He reiterated his desire for a just peace that prevents Russia from launching future aggressions.

During the envoys' visit, Putin and Zelenskyy reportedly agreed to a three-day halt on attacks on each other's capitals. This temporary pause coincided with the envoys' travel, which involved flying to Poland and then taking a train to Kyiv after their plane could not land directly.

Kushner mentioned that in Moscow, the US delegation discussed proposals that had not been fruitful so far, alongside considering what is needed for "lasting peace." He described the talks with Putin as "very good," with both sides asking many questions.

Zelenskyy also announced that a trilateral meeting involving officials from Ukraine, Europe, and the United States would be held soon to advance peace negotiations. The envoys were welcomed by Zelenskyy near St. Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv.
